title: School Timetable Update
content: Dear students, tomorrow's computer lab period has been moved to 10:00 AM. Please report to the lab on time. — School Office
explanation: This is a normal school announcement from the school's official-looking domain. Not every message is a threat. Still, checking the sender is a good habit.

title: You Won a New Phone!
content: CONGRATULATIONS!!! You have won a brand-new smartphone! Click here NOW to claim your prize. This offer expires in 5 minutes!
explanation: This message uses excitement, urgency and an unbelievable prize to make you act without thinking. Treat unexpected prizes and urgent links with suspicion.

title: Free Game Coins Pop-up
content: CONGRATULATIONS! You have been selected for 5,000 FREE game coins! Click 'Claim Now' to add them to your account immediately!
explanation: A random pop-up promising free game currency is a common scam. Close it instead of clicking the reward.

title: Classmate Messages You
content: Hey! Are you coming to the science project group after school? We're meeting in the library at 4 PM.
explanation: This is a normal message from a classmate about schoolwork. It does not ask for a password, OTP or money.

title: Unknown USB Drive
content: USB device detected: EXAM_NOTES_FREE. This device is ready to use.
explanation: An unknown USB drive can contain harmful software. A tempting name does not make it safe. Do not open it just because it promises notes or games.

title: Urgent Account Password Reset
content: We detected unusual activity on your account. Your password needs to be reset immediately. Click the link below to secure your account.
explanation: Urgent password-reset messages can be phishing. Do not use the link in the message. Open the real app or website yourself to check your account.

title: Friend Asks for Your OTP
content: Hey, I accidentally logged into your account on my phone. Can you send me the OTP you just received? I need it quickly!
explanation: Never share an OTP, even with someone claiming to be your friend. Contact your friend another way to check whether the message is really from them.

title: Leaked Exam Paper
content: URGENT: Tomorrow's question paper has been leaked! Download it before the link expires in 2 hours. Don't tell your teachers!
explanation: The message uses urgency and secrecy to pressure you. A supposed leaked question paper is a strong reason not to click an unknown download link.

title: Security Update Available
content: A security update is ready for your laptop. It fixes known security problems and requires a restart after installation.
explanation: Genuine security updates help protect devices from known problems. This is a legitimate security action, so not every alert should be ignored.

title: Fake Instagram Login
content: Your session has expired. Log in again to continue. The page looks like Instagram, but the address bar shows: instagram-login.security-check.example
explanation: The page may look real, but the address is not the official Instagram website. Check the URL before entering a password.

title: Free Snack QR Code
content: A poster near the school canteen says: 'SCAN TO GET A FREE SNACK! Limited offer for students!' The QR code leads to: student-snacks-rewards.example/claim
explanation: QR codes can hide the destination until you scan them. Check where the code leads and whether the offer is genuine before entering information.

title: Teacher Asks for Your Password
content: Hi, I am having trouble with my school account. Please send me your login password so I can check something before tomorrow's class. — Ms. Anita
explanation: A teacher or school staff member should not need your personal password. Even if the sender address looks familiar, verify the request through a known school contact method.

title: Account Verification Warning
content: Your account will be suspended in 24 hours unless you verify it. Use the link below to confirm your account.
explanation: The message creates urgency and provides a suspicious link. If you are worried about your account, open the real app yourself and check for security alerts there.

title: Someone Claims to Be School IT
content: Hi, this is the school IT team. We need to check your laptop for a security problem. Please install this tool now. It will only take a minute.
explanation: Unexpected requests to install software should be verified first. Contact the school through a known official channel rather than trusting the unknown number.

title: Streaming Subscription Alert
content: Your streaming subscription has been renewed for ₹1,499. If this wasn't you, click here immediately to cancel and get a refund within 24 hours.
explanation: Scammers often use a fake payment or refund message to make you click quickly. Check the real service through its official app or website instead.

title: You Won a Scholarship
content: Congratulations! You have been selected for a ₹50,000 student scholarship. To claim it, click the link and submit your ID document, bank details and other personal information.
explanation: An unexpected scholarship message asking for sensitive information should be verified independently. Find the organisation's real website yourself before sharing documents or financial information.

title: Friend Sends a Strange Link
content: OMG! This website shows who has viewed your profile! You HAVE to try it. Just log in with your account: profile-viewers.example
explanation: A friend's account could have been hacked. Strange links and requests to log in should be checked with the friend through another method before opening them.

title: Fake Virus Warning
content: WARNING! 3 viruses found on your laptop! Your photos and files are at risk. Download 'SecureGuard' now to remove the threats. Act within 30 minutes!
explanation: A scary browser pop-up can be designed to make you panic and download malware. Close it and, if worried, check your real security software.

title: School Competition QR Code
content: A professional-looking poster near the school gate advertises a 'National Young Coders Challenge'. The QR code asks for your name, phone number, school name and student ID.
explanation: A professional-looking poster can still be fake. Verify the competition with your school or the organiser's known official website before sharing personal information.

title: Library Fine Notice
content: You have an overdue library book and a fine of ₹150 has been added to your student account. Please click the link below to pay immediately.
explanation: The message looks like it could be real, but you should still verify it. Check your actual library account or ask the library before making a payment.

title: Parent Needs Money Urgently
content: I'm outside and my phone is about to die. Please send ₹2,000 to this UPI ID right now. It's urgent. I'll explain when I get home.
explanation: Someone can impersonate a family member online. Never send money just because a message sounds urgent. Call your parent using their usual number to confirm.

title: Prize From a Student Competition
content: Congratulations! You have won ₹25,000 in the Future Students Competition. To receive the prize, send your bank account details and a photo of your ID.
explanation: Unexpected prize messages can be scams. Verify the competition and its official contact details before sharing identity or financial information.

title: Study Guide Is an EXE File
content: Here's the maths study guide for tomorrow! I put it in the shared folder. It's a .exe file, but don't worry, it just contains the PDFs.
explanation: A study guide being sent as an executable file is unusual. Do not open it just because a classmate says it is safe. Verify with the classmate through another channel first.

title: Cloud Storage Almost Full
content: Your cloud storage is 99% full! Your photos and school files may be deleted unless you upgrade now for just ₹249/month.
explanation: Scammers create urgency around important files to make people pay or click. Check your real storage status in the official app or website.

title: School Photo Submission
content: Reminder: Please submit your photo for the school ID card by Friday. Use the school portal to upload it.
explanation: This is a normal school message from the official school domain. It is a useful reminder that legitimate messages also appear in the game.

title: Quick Money Trading Scheme
content: I made ₹10,000 this week using a secret trading app! Send me ₹500 and I'll show you how to double it. Guaranteed profit!
explanation: Promises of guaranteed quick money are a common scam. Do not send money to strangers promising easy profits.

title: Password Reuse Warning
content: Your password is being used on 3 different websites. If one website is hacked, someone could try the same password on your other accounts.
explanation: Using the same password everywhere is risky. If one account is compromised, attackers may try that password on your other accounts.

title: Turn On Two-Step Verification
content: Protect your account with two-step verification. This adds another check after your password when you sign in.
explanation: Two-step verification adds another layer of protection. A good cybersecurity habit is to enable it when an account supports it.

title: Free ₹5,000 Shopping Voucher
content: CONGRATULATIONS! Complete this 2-minute survey and win a ₹5,000 shopping voucher! Only a few vouchers left!
explanation: Unexpected prize surveys can collect personal information or lead to scams. Close the pop-up instead of rushing to claim the reward.

title: Online Game Reward Scam
content: You have been selected for a free game skin! Log in with your game username and password to claim it before the offer expires.
explanation: Free skins and game rewards are common bait for stealing passwords. Do not enter your login details through an unexpected message.

title: School Wi-Fi Available
content: A Wi-Fi network called 'GreenValley_Free' is available. It looks similar to the school's official network 'GreenValley-Secure'.
explanation: A network name can be copied to look official. Check with school staff or the official network information before connecting.

title: Suspicious Login Detected
content: A new login was detected from a device you do not recognise. Was this you?
explanation: An unfamiliar login deserves attention. Review the account activity and secure the account if the login was not yours.

title: New Sign-In to Your Google Account
content: A new device just signed in to your Google account. If this was not you, review your account security settings.

metadata.subject: New sign-in to your Google Account

explanation: This is a legitimate security alert. Checking account activity is useful when you see an unfamiliar sign-in.

title: Classmate Shares Homework
content: Hey, I shared the history project slides with you on SchoolDrive. Let me know if you can access them!
explanation: This is a normal classmate message about schoolwork. It does not ask for a password, OTP or money.

title: Your Password Was Leaked
content: Your email address appeared in a data breach. Change your password immediately using the secure link below.
explanation: A breach warning can be real, but scammers also use fake breach alerts. Check the service directly instead of clicking the message link.

title: School Fundraiser Message
content: Hi! We're collecting ₹100 for a school charity drive. Please donate using this payment link. The fundraiser is only open today!
explanation: Even a message that appears to come from school should be verified before sending money. Check with the Student Council or school through an official channel.

title: School Device Setup
content: School Device Setup: this will allow the school's IT team to manage certain settings on this laptop.
explanation: Software that can manage device settings should only be installed after confirming that it is really from your school. Verify with school IT first.

title: Unexpected School Supplies Bill
content: Invoice #8847: Your school owes ₹3,425 for supplies ordered on 15/08/2026. Payment is due immediately. Click to view the invoice.
explanation: If you or your school did not expect the order, do not pay just because an email says you owe money. Verify the order through a known contact.

title: Fake Browser Update
content: Your browser is out of date. Download the latest security update now to keep browsing safely.
explanation: Fake browser updates can install malware. Check for updates through the browser's own settings rather than downloading from a pop-up.

title: Friend Request From a New Account
content: A new account using your friend's name and profile photo wants to connect. The account was created last week and has very little information.
explanation: Someone can create an account using another person's name and photo. Check the profile and confirm the person's identity through another channel before accepting.
